pr_title: ddl: loose alter column with foreign key in some cases
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/22820

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:
when changing a column with FK, if its field type hasn't been changed, it can be allowed to run.

For MySQL:
For varchar type, a column with FK can also be allowed to expand the flen size.
But for decimal type, a column with FK can't be allowed to modify the flen&decimal in any case.

**It needs more detailed control here, in this PR, we just banned all the changes of field type in a column with FK.**

### Related changes

- PR to update `pingcap/docs`/`pingcap/docs-cn`:
- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test
- Integration test

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- ddl: loose alter column with fk in some cases.

issue_context.title: ddl: drop not null will refuse to run when there is foreign key on it
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)
```
CREATE TABLE users (
id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
doc JSON
);
CREATE TABLE orders (
id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
user_id INT NOT NULL,
doc JSON,
FOREIGN KEY fk_user_id (user_id) REFERENCES users(id)
);

alter table orders modify user_id int null;
```

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
```
success
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
```
ERROR 3780 (HY000): Referencing column 'user_id' in foreign key constraint 'fk_user_id' are incompatible
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
master
5.0.0-rc
4.0.x
comments:
mysql can run it without any error
```
mysql> alter table orders modify user_id int null;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.02 sec)
Records: 0  Duplicates: 0  Warnings: 0
```

Actually, although we do not support FK, for this case above, orders.user_id can be changed as NULL, it has nothing conflict with FK constraint.

Because for the latter insert into orders, the NULL value in the user_id field will skip the check with the foreign table.
